expected.because: 31 Dec 2025 is still the 2025 policy. Its 4.2 keeps the specialist-referral exception, the referral is on file, so the referral precedent applies and nothing is missing.
1 Jan 2026 is the 2026 policy, which removed the referral exception: the referral precedent no longer applies, and the clause now needs a retroactive request plus a necessity letter.

results.purpose: filed exactly at the 2026 timely-filing limit (90 days)

expected.because: The 2026 limit is 90 days and the claim was filed on day 90, which is not late. Proof of timely filing is on file. The 180-day precedent was learned under the old clause and does not carry over.

results.purpose: filed one day past the 2026 timely-filing limit

expected.because: Day 91 exceeds the 90-day limit in force on the service date: the governing terms leave no appeal basis.

results.purpose: enrolled exactly the required 9 months under the 2026 policy

expected.because: 2026 section 3.2 requires 9 months; 9 is not fewer than 9, so the waiting period is met. The enrollment record is on file and the 2026 precedent applies.

results.purpose: one month short of the 2026 waiting period

expected.because: 8 months is fewer than the 9 required by the 2026 policy: no basis for appeal. Whether the precedent 'applies' is ambiguous here, so it is not scored.

results.purpose: negation (it is NOT a prior-authorization denial)

expected.because: The stated reason is a coding mismatch, with the authorization explicitly excluded. Section 9.4 needs an itemized bill (on file) and a corrected coding submission (missing). The coding precedent is valid in every version.

results.purpose: negation of two other reasons, duplicate claim

expected.because: Duplicate submission; the itemized bill (on file) is what section 9.5 asks for to show distinct services. The duplicate precedent is valid in 2026.

results.purpose: paraphrase with no section and no keyword from the taxonomy

expected.because: Advance approval not obtained is prior authorization. Under the 2025 policy the referral exception holds and its precedent applies, so the specialist referral is what is missing.

results.purpose: durable equipment, a precedent learned in 2025 that is still valid in 2026

expected.because: 2026 section 5.1 caps sessions at 12 and asks for a necessity letter and progress notes, both on file. The old progress-notes-only precedent was learned under the 20-session clause and does not apply; the 2026 precedent does.

generalization.authorship: Written by the AI assistant that helped build the system, before any run, from the policy text. Separately authored, not independent. Sample is small and synthetic.

notes: Baseline RAG + findings (the information-parity comparison) was NOT run: the free Groq tier's daily token limit (200,000) was exhausted earlier the same day and every attempt returned a provider rate-limit error. The code is in place; it is the comparison that most needs running.
Letters without a section number need a live model call; where the provider was unavailable the unseen-case check reports them as not evaluated, not as failures.
